clue.text: His writing career started out with inclinations after vainglory

definitions.text: His writing career started out with inclinations after vainglory

parts.words: His writing career started out with inclinations after vainglory
parts.note: a literary riddle: the novelist's breakthrough book was titled Vainglory, and his tree-and-slope surname splits into a conifer plus a word for inclines

explanation.surface: A writer whose career began with leanings toward vanity.
explanation.walkthrough: Ronald Firbank's novel Vainglory (1915) launched his career; 'inclinations' hints at BANK, a slope, after a FIR.
explanation.definitionFit: Ronald Firbank was the English novelist whose first full novel was Vainglory.

clue.text: Some illumination provided by Rattigan for 22 down

definitions.text: Some illumination provided by Rattigan for 22 down

parts.words: Some illumination provided by Rattigan for 22 down
parts.note: a row of lights guiding aircraft in to land, which is also the title of Rattigan's wartime RAF play

explanation.definitionFit: A flare path is a line of lights marking a runway for airmen; Terence Rattigan's 1942 play takes that title.

clue.text: Firmness of purpose alien to Hamlet's spirit and apparently to his solid flesh

definitions.text: Firmness of purpose alien to Hamlet's spirit

explanation.definitionFit: Determination is what Hamlet lacks, and he wishes his too solid flesh would melt and dissolve itself into a dew.

clue.text: Gap author might produce in original manuscript

indicators.note: might produce suggests the letters of the two words are reworked into something new

explanation.surface: A missing passage that a writer could create in a first draft.
explanation.definitionFit: An autograph is a document in the writer's own hand.

clue.text: Mickey Spillane invited a deadly one

definitions.text: Mickey Spillane invited a deadly one

parts.words: Mickey Spillane invited a deadly one
parts.note: plays on the title of Spillane's thriller, an invitation to a lethal embrace

explanation.definitionFit: Spillane's Mike Hammer novel is Kiss Me, Deadly, an invitation to a deadly smooch.

clue.text: "They sway'd about upon a rocking horse, / And thought it " (Keats)

definitions.text: "They sway'd about upon a rocking horse, / And thought it " (Keats)

parts.words: "They sway'd about upon a rocking horse, / And thought it " (Keats)
parts.note: a gap-fill: Keats in Sleep and Poetry mocks poets who mistook a nursery toy for the winged steed of the Muses

explanation.walkthrough: The missing word ends the couplet from Keats's Sleep and Poetry.
explanation.definitionFit: The winged horse of Greek myth is the emblem of poetic inspiration, which the mocked poets imagined they rode.

clue.text: Extra piles to be sorted out for sculptor

indicators.note: to be sorted out says the letters of the two words are put in a new order

explanation.surface: Surplus heaps needing tidying for an artist who carves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be sorted out' rearranges EXTRA PILES.
explanation.definitionFit: Praxiteles was the great Athenian sculptor of the fourth century BC.

clue.text: Moneylender bent and twisted in Dickens, but right in Gide

definitions.text: Moneylender bent and twisted in Dickens

explanation.surface: A crooked usurer in Dickens who becomes correct when set in Gide.
explanation.walkthrough: Arthur Gride is the miserly moneylender in Nicholas Nickleby.
explanation.definitionFit: Arthur Gride is the stooped, grasping usurer of Nicholas Nickleby.

clue.text: Sport in school hospital for Scandinavian writers

indicators.note: in places the word for sport inside the word for the school sickbay

parts.note: san, short for sanatorium, is the sickroom at a British boarding school
a game is a sport

explanation.surface: Games played in the school infirmary for Norse authors.
explanation.definitionFit: Sagamen were the Norse tellers and writers of sagas.

clue.text: Angus Wilson's liberal humanist with connections to (9)

definitions.text: Angus Wilson's liberal humanist with connections to (9)

parts.words: Angus Wilson's liberal humanist with connections to (9)
parts.note: points to the central figure of Wilson's Hemlock and After, a humane novelist

explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference at the end appears damaged in the source; the clue rests on Wilson's character Bernard Sands.
explanation.definitionFit: Bernard Sands, the liberal novelist at the centre of Angus Wilson's Hemlock and After, gives the surname.

clue.text: Talent in O'Hara's set-piece stories ()

indicators.note: in signals that the answer sits inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A gift on display in John O'Hara's carefully staged stories.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' points inside O'HARA'S SET-piece, where ASSET runs across the words; 'stories' merely completes the picture.
explanation.definitionFit: A talent is a valuable quality, something counted as a resource in one's favour.

clue.text: Hanging around after The Raj Quartet (7)

explanation.definitionFit: To stay on is to linger when others have left; Paul Scott's novel of that title followed his Raj Quartet.

clue.text: Guy mistakenly associated waith Leo in oration

indicators.note: mistakenly suggests the two names have been wrongly put together, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A man named Guy wrongly linked with one called Leo in a speech.
explanation.definitionFit: A eulogy is a formal speech of praise, a kind of oration.

clue.text: Tipped lid of Austen character, causing problems

indicators.note: tipped means the word lid is turned over and read backwards

parts.note: Emma, heroine of Jane Austen's novel, with the possessive S from 'of'

explanation.surface: Upsetting the hat of a Jane Austen heroine causes trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tipped' turns LID into DIL; Emma's lid is DIL plus EMMA'S.
explanation.definitionFit: Dilemmas are awkward choices between alternatives, a kind of difficulty.

clue.text: Address to conspirator by Barrie

explanation.definitionFit: Opening a letter to Caesar's assassin would read thus, and it is also the title of J. M. Barrie's 1917 play.

clue.text: Venue associated with blood in the Spanish of Ibañez

definitions.text: associated with blood in the Spanish of Ibañez

explanation.walkthrough: Arena is Spanish for sand, as in Blasco Ibáñez's bullfighting novel.
explanation.definitionFit: An arena is a place for contests; Blasco Ibáñez's novel Sangre y arena pairs blood with sand.

clue.text: Agatha Christie's can remember

parts.note: completes the title of a late Christie novel about creatures proverbial for memory

explanation.definitionFit: Christie's 1972 Poirot novel is titled Elephants Can Remember, after the proverbial long memory of the beasts.

clue.text: Working man in Rome (not necessarily with publisher)

definitions.text: Working man in Rome (not necessarily with publisher)

parts.words: Working man in Rome (not necessarily with publisher)
parts.note: Latin for man the maker, also a Max Frisch novel, whose second word is the name of a London publishing house

explanation.definitionFit: Homo faber is Latin for man the maker, and the title of Max Frisch's novel; Faber is also a publisher.

clue.text: Hall Caine's (or Daphne du Maurier's?) fall-guy

explanation.definitionFit: Both Hall Caine and Daphne du Maurier wrote novels with this title, and it means one blamed for others' faults.

clue.text: May be a US novelist, by the sound of it

indicators.note: by the sound of it says the word for the tree is heard as a homophone

parts.note: may is another name for the hawthorn tree and its blossom

explanation.surface: Perhaps an American writer, judging by what one hears.
explanation.walkthrough: May, the springtime blossom, is the hawthorn; said aloud it gives Nathaniel Hawthorne.
explanation.definitionFit: Nathaniel Hawthorne wrote The Scarlet Letter, a classic of American fiction.

clue.text: See Wodehouse character court saint with hesitation- (9)

parts.note: to court is to woo
er is the sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: A Wodehouse figure courts a holy man, hesitating.
explanation.walkthrough: Bertie Wooster is Jeeves's employer in Wodehouse's stories.
explanation.definitionFit: Bertie Wooster is P. G. Wodehouse's amiable idle hero.

clue.text: Many with song identify Hemingway heroine

parts.note: M, the Roman numeral for a thousand, stands for many
an aria is a song in an opera

explanation.surface: Many people singing pick out a woman from a Hemingway novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Maria is the young Spanish woman loved by Robert Jordan in For Whom the Bell Tolls.

clue.text: Studying where Wilde retired for a while to do some quiet work

parts.words: where Wilde retired for a while to do some quiet work
parts.note: ironic description of Oscar Wilde's imprisonment in the gaol of a Berkshire town

explanation.surface: A scholar recalls where Oscar Wilde spent time on peaceful labour.
explanation.walkthrough: Wilde served hard labour in Reading Gaol, here wryly called retiring to do quiet work.
explanation.definitionFit: Reading means perusing books, a kind of study; Reading is also the town with the gaol where Wilde was held.

clue.text: Duke of Milan may do well with ring

parts.note: to prosper is to do well
O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: An Italian duke may thrive wearing a ring.
explanation.definitionFit: Prospero, the magician of The Tempest, is the rightful Duke of Milan.

clue.text: Cooper's guide too early to come in on 1 down

definitions.text: Cooper's guide too early to come in on 1 down

parts.words: Cooper's guide too early to come in on 1 down
parts.note: Fenimore Cooper's sea novel names a guide; a sea guide of his day predates aircraft landing by runway lights

explanation.definitionFit: James Fenimore Cooper's novel The Pilot concerns a navigator who guides ships, long before airmen landed by flare paths.

clue.text: Shepherdess with ideas above her station ()

definitions.text: Shepherdess with ideas above her station ()

parts.words: Shepherdess with ideas above her station ()
parts.note: the scornful country girl in As You Like It who loves a disguised noblewoman

explanation.definitionFit: Phebe, the disdainful shepherdess of As You Like It, falls for Rosalind disguised as a youth.

clue.text: "The western wave was all —, / The day was well nigh done!" (Coleridge)

definitions.text: "The western wave was all —, / The day was well nigh done!" (Coleridge)

parts.words: "The western wave was all —, / The day was well nigh done!" (Coleridge)
parts.note: a gap-fill from The Rime of the Ancient Mariner, where the sunset sets the sea ablaze

explanation.definitionFit: In the Ancient Mariner the setting sun makes the western sea look on fire.

clue.text: She agreed to Acton out of sibling solidarity

definitions.text: She agreed to Acton out of sibling solidarity

parts.words: She agreed to Acton out of sibling solidarity
parts.note: the youngest Bronte sister took a male pen-name to match those of her sisters

explanation.definitionFit: Anne Brontë published as Acton Bell, alongside Currer and Ellis Bell.

clue.text: Poet, politician, patron, and friend of Pope who sounds less than a heavyweight

definitions.text: Poet, politician, patron, and friend of Pope

indicators.note: sounds signals that the phrase is to be heard rather than spelt

parts.note: a little ton, something weighing less than a ton

explanation.surface: An eighteenth-century man of letters whose name suggests a featherweight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'who' is a link; LITTLE TON spoken aloud gives the surname.
explanation.definitionFit: George Lyttelton was a poet and statesman, patron of Fielding and Thomson and friend of Alexander Pope.

clue.text: Librettist at start of Bellini opera is too optimistic ()

indicators.note: at start of takes the opening letter of each of the following words

explanation.surface: A librettist for a Bellini opera is too hopeful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at start of' covers all five words from Bellini to optimistic. Arrigo Boito wrote the libretti for Verdi's Otello and Falstaff.
explanation.definitionFit: Arrigo Boito was an Italian poet who wrote opera texts for Verdi.

clue.text: Described by Hazlitt as "pictures of nothing and very like"

definitions.text: Described by Hazlitt as "pictures of nothing and very like"

parts.words: Described by Hazlitt as "pictures of nothing and very like"
parts.note: Hazlitt's jibe at the hazy landscapes of the great English painter of light

explanation.definitionFit: Hazlitt's remark referred to J. M. W. Turner's late paintings, so the pictures are Turners.

clue.text: Well-known DJ. Also poet, critic and novelist

explanation.definitionFit: D. J. Enright, known by his initials, was an English poet, critic and novelist.
